title: Decoding scanned tape tracks
statement: Let $A$ be a finite alphabet with decidable equality, let $e$ embed the Booleans into $A$, let $k$ be a natural number, let $x$ be a binary word, and let $c$ be a configuration over $A$ on the input obtained by applying $e$ to each bit of $x$. For every tape index $i<k$, decoding the family of bits read from the encoded configuration's tracks indexed by symbols of $A$ recovers exactly the possibly blank symbol under tape $i$'s head in $c$.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is a configuration over $A$ on the symbolwise image of $x$
replaced:
Let $c$ be a configuration of a $k$-tape machine over a finite alphabet $A$ on the
symbolwise embedding of a binary word. For every logical tape index $i < k$, decoding
the family of bits scanned on the tracks of block $i$ in the encoded configuration
yields exactly the symbol scanned by $c$ on tape $i$.
